title: Cleaning Services Contract | Free Word Template
description: Free cleaning services contract: define scope, schedule, fees, supplies and cancellation for residential or commercial cleaning.
lead: A contract between a cleaner/cleaning company and a client (residential or commercial) listing cleaning tasks, frequency/schedule, rates, payment terms, supplies, cancellation and access details.
introParagraphs: A cleaning services contract (or house cleaning agreement) defines what the cleaner will do, how often, what areas/tasks are included (and excluded), rates, payment terms, key/access arrangements, supplies provided, and cancellation policy.
Clear scope prevents 'I thought you did the windows' disputes. Explicitly list what is not included (deep cleans, exterior windows, carpet shampoo, dishes, laundry) and what costs extra.
bullets: Cleaner and client
Cleaner/business name, contact and insurance info; client name; property address and entry details (key, alarm code, entry method).
Scope of services

Which rooms/areas, included tasks per visit (dust, vacuum, mop, bathrooms, kitchen, bins, linens), frequency (weekly, bi-weekly, monthly, one-off deep clean), and exclusions (windows, carpets, exterior, hazardous materials).
Schedule and access
Day/time of visits, who is home, key/access arrangements, alarm handling, pet instructions, and what happens if client is not home.
Fees and payment
Rate per visit/hourly, billing cadence (per visit or monthly), payment method, late/cancellation fee (typically 24-48 hour notice required), and supplies (cleaner provides vs client provides).
Liability and terms
Insurance confirmation (bonded/insured), damage/theft policy, client responsibility for valuables, termination notice period (typically 7-30 days), and any satisfaction guarantee/re-clean policy.
howTo: Walk through the property together
Do a walk-through before the first clean to agree on scope, priorities and tricky areas.
List inclusions and exclusions
Be explicit about what is and is not included; add-on services priced separately.
Arrange access safely
Use a key-safe or lockbox rather than leaving keys under mats; document alarm disarm procedure.
Set cancellation policy
24-48 hours notice for cancellations; late cancellations charged a fee.
Review after first clean
Do a post-clean walk-through and adjust scope/expectations before setting the recurring schedule.
related: Master services agreement for recurring commercial work.
If there are pets on the property.
faq: Should the cleaner be bonded and insured?
Yes — confirm general liability and (if employees) workers comp; bond coverage protects against theft allegations.
Who provides supplies?
It varies; many cleaners bring their own, some prefer client supplies for chemical sensitivities. State clearly.
Do I need to be home?
Most recurring services work while the client is out — agree on key/access procedures in advance.
What about damages?
Good cleaners will acknowledge and fix/reimburse for accidental damage; uninsured cleaners create risk.
Do I need a contract for one-off cleans?
Short booking terms + email confirmation is enough; recurring services benefit from a signed contract.

title: Coaching Agreement | Free Word Template
description: Free coaching agreement: set package, sessions, fees, cancellation and responsibilities for life/business/executive coaching.
lead: An agreement between a coach and client defining the coaching package, session cadence and length, fees, payment schedule, cancellation/reschedule policy, confidentiality and coaching boundaries.
introParagraphs: A coaching agreement sets out the expectations between a coach (life, business, executive, career, health) and client. It covers the package (number of sessions, length, period), fees, scheduling, cancellation policy, confidentiality, and the important disclaimer that coaching is not therapy, medical, legal or financial advice.
Good coaches set clear boundaries — coaching goals are co-created with the client, results depend on client action, and coaches do not diagnose or treat mental health conditions.
bullets: Coach and client
Coach name and credentials; client name; agreement start date; session delivery method (phone, video, in-person).
Coaching package
Number of sessions, session length (e.g. 60 minutes), session cadence (weekly/bi-weekly), and the duration of the engagement (e.g. 3 months, 6 months).
Fees and payment
Total package fee, payment plan (upfront or monthly instalments), accepted payment methods, and refund policy.
Scheduling and cancellation
How sessions are scheduled, required notice to reschedule (typically 24 hours), late-cancellation/no-show policy (session is forfeited), and session expiration.
Boundaries and disclaimer
Confidentiality (with standard exceptions for harm/illegal activity), disclaimer that coaching is not therapy/medical/legal/financial advice, client responsibility for action, and recording policy.
howTo: Hold a discovery call first
Make sure there is a fit before signing; set expectations for what coaching can and cannot do.
Set session cadence and length
60-minute weekly sessions is typical; include session expiry (unused sessions expire at end of engagement).
State fees clearly
Total package vs instalments; include late-payment terms and whether packages auto-renew.
Include a clear disclaimer
Coaching is not a substitute for mental health or licensed professional services; refer to therapists/doctors/lawyers when needed.
Sign before first session
Both parties sign; coach and client each get a copy. Review package at engagement end.
related: Fitness coaching cousin of this agreement.
For advisory/consulting rather than pure coaching.
For regulated professionals who also coach.
faq: Is coaching the same as therapy?
No — therapy treats mental health conditions; coaching supports goal achievement and personal growth. Refer clients to therapists when appropriate.
Should I offer refunds?
Typically not for completed sessions; unused sessions may be refunded within limits. Be explicit.
Do I need insurance?
Professional liability insurance for coaches is recommended — inexpensive and protects if advice is alleged to cause harm.
Can I record sessions?
Only with client explicit written consent; state recording policy in the agreement.
Do I need certification?
Certification is not legally required for coaching in most places, but ethics bodies (ICF) require their own credentialing/agreements.

title: Tutoring Agreement | Free Word Template
description: Free tutoring agreement: set subject, sessions, rates, cancellation and expectations between tutor and student/parent.
lead: An agreement between a tutor and student (or parent/guardian for a minor) covering subject, session length/frequency, rate, location (in-person/online), payment terms, cancellation policy and progress expectations.
introParagraphs: A tutoring agreement clarifies expectations for private tutoring: subject(s), session length and frequency, rate per session, payment schedule, cancellation policy, location (in-person/online), what the student is expected to bring/do between sessions, and how progress is communicated.
For minor students, the parent/guardian signs; include a safety/conduct clause and clearly state tutoring does not guarantee grades — results depend on student effort.
bullets: Tutor and client
Tutor name, subject expertise; student name and age; parent/guardian name (if minor); contact details.
Subject and sessions
Subject(s) and level (e.g. GCSE maths, SAT prep, university chemistry), session length (e.g. 60 or 90 minutes), frequency (weekly, twice-weekly), start date and engagement length.
Location and format
In-person address/online platform, who provides materials, tech requirements for online sessions, and parent observation policy (for minors).
Fees and payment
Hourly/session rate, payment schedule (per session, weekly, monthly in advance), accepted payment methods, late-payment fee, and package discounts.
Cancellation and expectations

Required cancellation notice (typically 24 hours), no-show/late-cancellation policy (session charged), student preparation expectations, parent communication/updates, and disclaimer that grades depend on student effort.
howTo: Run a diagnostic session
Assess current level and agree specific goals before signing.
Set clear cancellation terms
24-hour notice; last-minute cancellations/no-shows forfeit the session.
Agree on materials/platform
State who provides textbooks, practice tests, online tools; confirm Zoom/Teams accounts for online sessions.
Be realistic about results
Do not promise specific grades; frame progress around effort and measurable milestones.
Invoice on a schedule
Bill weekly/monthly in advance to prevent collection issues; offer package discounts for block bookings.
related: Another parent-signed agreement for services to children.
For tutors working through agencies or longer engagements.
faq: Do I need a DBS/background check?
For tutoring minors in many countries, a background check (DBS in UK) is expected/required by most parents even if not legally mandated.
Who provides materials?
Tutors often recommend a textbook and provide worksheets/practice tests; state in the agreement.
Do I guarantee grades?
No — make clear in the agreement that outcomes depend on student effort and practice between sessions.
Can a parent sit in?
Often yes, especially for younger students — state your policy; one-way observation is less disruptive than active participation.
What about make-up sessions?
Offer make-up sessions for cancellations with sufficient notice; last-minute cancellations are forfeited.

title: Personal Training Agreement | Free Word Template
description: Free personal training agreement: set sessions, fees, cancellation, PAR-Q and liability terms for personal training.
lead: An agreement between a personal trainer and client covering session package, schedule, fees, cancellation policy, health screening (PAR-Q), liability waiver and fitness-results disclaimer.
introParagraphs: A personal training agreement sets the terms between trainer and client: package (number of sessions, length, frequency), fees, scheduling, cancellation policy, gym location, required health screening, a liability waiver, and a disclaimer that results depend on client adherence to exercise and nutrition.
Always require a PAR-Q (Physical Activity Readiness Questionnaire) and doctor clearance if indicated; include a liability waiver and verify your insurance covers the training setting.
bullets: Trainer and client
Trainer name/certifications; client name and contact; start date; gym/facility location or online training.
Sessions and package
Number of sessions, session length (e.g. 60 min), frequency (1-5x/week), and package expiration date (unused sessions typically expire).
Fees and payment
Package price or per-session rate, payment schedule (upfront, monthly, per session), accepted payment methods, late payment and refund policy.
Health screening and safety
PAR-Q requirement, doctor clearance if needed, client disclosure of injuries/conditions, cancellation due to illness/injury, and emergency contact.
Cancellation, waiver and disclaimer
Late-cancellation policy (often 24 hours; charge for no-shows), liability waiver/assumption of risk, disclaimer that results depend on nutrition/adherence, and termination terms.
howTo: Start with a PAR-Q
Have the client fill out a PAR-Q before the first session; require doctor clearance for moderate/high-risk answers.
Define the package
Specify sessions, length, expiration and any add-ons (nutrition plans, online check-ins).
Set cancellation rules
24-hour notice for cancellations; late cancellations/no-shows count as a used session.
Include a waiver
Clients assume the risk of exercise; waiver must be clear but cannot waive gross negligence.
Carry proper insurance
Carry personal trainer liability insurance; work in insured facilities where possible.
related: Standalone activity waiver; often bundled into PT agreements.
For health/life coaching rather than hands-on training.
faq: Do I need certification?
Most gyms require certification (NASM, ACE, ACSM); independent trainers should carry it for credibility and insurance.
Do I need insurance?
Yes — professional and general liability insurance for trainers is a must; clients can be injured.
Do I need a PAR-Q for every client?
Yes — industry best practice; protects both trainer and client by flagging health risks.
Can I guarantee weight loss?
No — results depend on diet, adherence and individual factors; avoid guarantees in the agreement.
What if a client is injured?
Stop activity, follow emergency procedures, document, and notify insurer promptly.

title: Pet Sitting Agreement | Free Word Template
description: Free pet sitting agreement: set care instructions, fees, vet authorisation, keys and liability for pet sitters.
lead: An agreement between a pet owner and a pet sitter covering pet details, care instructions (feeding, walks, meds), dates, fees, key pickup/return, vet authorisation and liability.
introParagraphs: A pet sitting agreement (or dog-sitting contract) tells the sitter exactly how to care for each pet — feeding schedule, medications, walks, playtime, emergency contact, and authorised vet. It also covers payment, key access, house rules, cancellation terms and liability.
Pets cannot communicate issues directly, so detailed written instructions are essential. Include a vet authorisation clause so the sitter can get emergency care if you cannot be reached.
bullets: Owner and sitter
Owner name, address and contact; sitter name; emergency contact for owner (friend/family); backup contact if owner is unreachable.
Pet details
Name, species, breed, age, sex, microchip number, vet name/clinic and phone for each pet; behaviour notes (aggression, anxiety, children/pets to avoid).
Care instructions
Feeding (what, when, how much), medications (dose, frequency), walks/exercise, playtime/litter/cleanup, allowed treats and forbidden foods, bedtime routine.
Dates, access and fees
Start and end dates, key pickup/return, alarm/house access, visits per day or live-in, total fee and deposit, payment method, cancellation/refund policy.
Vet authorisation and liability
Sitter is authorised to seek emergency vet care at owner expense; pet health disclosure; liability limits for accidents/illness; sitter is not responsible for pre-existing conditions.
howTo: Do a meet-and-greet first
Have sitter meet the pets before the booking; share personality quirks and routines.
Write detailed care instructions
Portion sizes, medication timing, forbidden foods (chocolate, grapes, xylitol), emergency commands.
Provide vet info and authorisation
Give vet name, address and 24h emergency clinic; sign authorisation so they can approve urgent treatment.
Handle keys securely
Exchange keys in person; agree return procedure; do not leave keys in obvious hiding places.
Confirm payment
Pay deposit to book; settle final payment on return; include cancellation/refund terms.
related: Similar in-home care agreement for children.
faq: Should sitters be bonded/insured?
Professional pet sitters carry liability insurance and bonding; hobby sitters may not — decide your risk tolerance.
Who pays vet bills in an emergency?
Owner pays — include a clause authorising the sitter to seek care up to a spending limit and confirming owner responsibility for bills.
What about bites or injuries?
Disclose any aggression history; owner is typically liable for pet bites. Sitters may want insurance.
Live-in vs drop-in visits?
State clearly whether sitter stays overnight, number of visits per day, and whether they may bring guests.
Do I pay if I come home early?
Typically yes for booked days unless agreed otherwise — sitters hold the time for you.
